claim: Darunavir (DRV) achieves high drug concentrations in vivo that are exceptional among potent HIV-1 protease inhibitors (PIs).
source: Darunavir (DRV) is exceptional among potent HIV-1 protease inhibitors (PIs) in high drug concentrations that are achieved in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key characteristic of DRV.

claim: Little is known about the de novo resistance pathway for DRV.
source: Little is known about the de novo resistance pathway for DRV.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract as a knowledge gap.

claim: Mutations accumulated through two pathways anchored by protease mutations I50V or I84V during selection for resistance to high drug concentrations against 10 PIs and DRV.
source: Mutations accumulated through two pathways (anchored by protease mutations I50V or I84V).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Small changes in the inhibitor P1'-equivalent position led to preferential use of one resistance pathway over the other.
source: Small changes in the inhibitor P1'-equivalent position led to preferential use of one pathway over the other.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by selection experiments showing pathway preference based on R1 group size.

claim: Changes in the inhibitor P2'-equivalent position determined differences in potency that were retained in the resistant viruses and that impacted the selected mutations.
source: Changes in the inhibitor P2'-equivalent position determined differences in potency that were retained in the resistant viruses and that impacted the selected mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Ki and EC50 measurements across different R2 groups.

claim: Viral variants from the two pathways showed differential selection of compensatory mutations in Gag cleavage sites.
source: Viral variants from the two pathways showed differential selection of compensatory mutations in Gag cleavage sites.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by sequencing data of Gag cleavage sites shown in Figure 7.

claim: The number of mutations selected increases with increasing drug concentration for protease inhibitors.
source: For protease inhibitors (PIs), the number of mutations selected increases with increasing drug concentration (Watkins et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The concentration of protease inhibitors in vivo is an important parameter in determining the genetic barrier to resistance.
source: Thus, the concentration of this drug class in vivo is an important parameter in determining the genetic barrier to resistance.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the relationship between drug concentration and mutation selection.

claim: The HIV-1 protease is a member of the aspartyl proteinase family.
source: The early identification of the retroviral protease as a member of the aspartyl proteinase family and the determination of a number of cleavage site sequences led to the development of first-generation PIs (PIs) that validated the HIV-1 protease as a drug target (Katoh et al., 1987; Richards et al., 1989; Seelmeier et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to early work on HIV-1 protease.

claim: First-generation PIs validated the HIV-1 protease as a drug target.
source: The early identification of the retroviral protease as a member of the aspartyl proteinase family and the determination of a number of cleavage site sequences led to the development of first-generation PIs (PIs) that validated the HIV-1 protease as a drug target (Katoh et al., 1987; Richards et al., 1989; Seelmeier et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to early work on protease inhibitors.

claim: A three-drug regimen including second-generation PIs achieved sustained suppression of viral load with no evolution of resistance.
source: A second generation of PIs was quickly developed for use in humans, becoming the third drug in a three-drug regimen that achieved sustained suppression of viral load with no evolution of resistance (Gulick et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Darunavir (DRV) is a fourth-generation PI.
source: These properties have been further enhanced with a fourth-generation PI, darunavir (DRV), which achieves a drug level in plasma (>1 µM) that is 1000-fold greater than its inhibitory activity in cell culture (Ali et al., 2010; Kurt Yilmaz et al., 2009; Nalam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated explicitly and supported by citations.

claim: DRV achieves a drug level in plasma (>1 µM) that is 1000-fold greater than its inhibitory activity in cell culture.
source: These properties have been further enhanced with a fourth-generation PI, darunavir (DRV), which achieves a drug level in plasma (>1 µM) that is 1000-fold greater than its inhibitory activity in cell culture (Ali et al., 2010; Kurt Yilmaz et al., 2009; Nalam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Initial trials of DRV monotherapy showed a modest increase in the loss of viral suppression relative to standard ART.
source: Although the initial trials of monotherapy showed a modest increase in the loss of viral suppression relative to standard ART, in the cases of virological failure there was no significant resistance to DRV detected in the rebound virus (Antinori et al., 2015; Arribas et al., 2012; Paton et al., 2015; Valantin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple clinical trials.

claim: In cases of virological failure during DRV monotherapy, there was no significant resistance to DRV detected in the rebound virus.
source: Although the initial trials of monotherapy showed a modest increase in the loss of viral suppression relative to standard ART, in the cases of virological failure there was no significant resistance to DRV detected in the rebound virus (Antinori et al., 2015; Arribas et al., 2012; Paton et al., 2015; Valantin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple clinical trials.

claim: The observed virological failure in DRV monotherapy is most easily attributed to issues of low drug exposure in specific participants.
source: Thus, the observed virological failure is most easily attributed to issues of low drug exposure in specific participants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of resistance mutations in virological failures.

claim: Several studies have shown that a PI can be part of a successful two drug therapy regimen.
source: In this regard, several studies have shown that a PI can be part of a successful two drug therapy regimen (Casado et al., 2020; Di Cristo et al., 2020; Hawkins et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2019; Vizcarra et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The appearance of DRV-resistant viruses during therapy failure has occurred in people who had previously experienced virological failure with other PIs.
source: The appearance of DRV-resistant viruses during therapy failure has occurred in people who had previously experienced virological failure with other PIs (de Meyer et al., 2008; Descamps et al., 2009; Pellegrin et al., 2008; Tremblay, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical observations.

claim: The pathway to DRV resistance was likely influenced by preexisting resistance to previous PIs.
source: In these cases, the pathway to DRV resistance was likely influenced by the preexisting resistance to the previous PI.
evidence: This is an inference based on the clinical observation of prior PI exposure.

claim: DRV resistance has been selected in cell culture.
source: DRV resistance has been selected in cell culture (Aoki et al., 2018; de Meyer et al., 2008; Koh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: High-level resistance to DRV was selected starting with either a mixture of highly resistant variants that were allowed to recombine or starting with a single PI-resistant strain, and in both cases, an I84V resistance pathway in the protease was observed.
source: High-level resistance was selected starting with either a mixture of highly resistant variants that were allowed to recombine or the selection was started with a single PI-resistant strain; in both cases, an I84V resistance pathway in the protease was observed.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous selection studies.

claim: There are no reports of selection of high-level resistance to DRV starting with an unmutated 'wildtype' virus.
source: However, there are no reports of selection of high-level resistance starting with an unmutated 'wildtype' virus.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature.

claim: An important concept in HIV-1 PI design is to avoid chemical moieties that extend outside of the substrate envelope.
source: An important concept in HIV-1 PI design is to avoid chemical moieties that extend outside of the substrate envelope, the shared volume in the protease active site that is occupied by natural protease substrates (King et al., 2004; King et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on inhibitor design.

claim: The substrate envelope is the shared volume in the protease active site that is occupied by natural protease substrates.
source: An important concept in HIV-1 PI design is to avoid chemical moieties that extend outside of the substrate envelope, the shared volume in the protease active site that is occupied by natural protease substrates (King et al., 2004; King et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations.

claim: A series of highly potent PIs based on DRV, UMASS-1 through -10, were designed that still fit within the substrate envelope.
source: We have previously designed a series of highly potent PIs based on DRV, UMASS-1 through -10, that still fit within the substrate envelope (Nalam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The designed fifth-generation inhibitors have modified chemical moieties that relative to DRV further fill the substrate envelope at the equivalent of the P1' and P2' positions.
source: The designed fifth-generation inhibitors have modified chemical moieties that relative to DRV further ﬁll the substrate envelope at the equivalent of the P1' and P2' positions (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: All UMASS inhibitors bind tightly to the wild-type HIV-1 protease with a Ki of less than 5 pM.
source: All bind tightly to the wild-type HIV-1 protease with a Ki of less than 5 pM.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: UMASS inhibitors retained robust binding to many multidrug-resistant protease variants and viral strains.
source: These inhibitors retained robust binding to many multidrug-resistant protease variants and viral strains.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Table 1.

claim: In most selections, either the I84V or the I50V mutation was largely fixed by the time the inhibitor concentration reached 10 nM in the culture.
source: In most of the selections, either the I84V or the I50V mutation was largely fixed by the time the inhibitor concentration reached 10 nM in the culture (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data shown in figures.

claim: Under continuous and escalating selective pressure, representing between 50 and 95 passages, the virus evolved to accumulate multiple mutations.
source: Under continuous and escalating selective pressure, representing between 50 and 95 passages, the virus evolved to accumulate multiple mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: In most cases, selection was carried out until the final concentration approximated that achieved by DRV in vivo.
source: In most cases, selection was carried out until the final concentration approximated that achieved by DRV in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental design.

claim: The EC50 values for DRV and the UMASS analogues ranged from 2.4 to 9.1 nM.
source: The EC50 values (the effective concentration needed at the time of virus production to reduce infectivity by 50%) for DRV and the UMASS analogues ranged from 2.4 to 9.1 nM, significantly more potent than the second- and third-generation PIs tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: DRV and UMASS analogues are significantly more potent than the second- and third-generation PIs tested.
source: The EC50 values (the effective concentration needed at the time of virus production to reduce infectivity by 50%) for DRV and the UMASS analogues ranged from 2.4 to 9.1 nM, significantly more potent than the second- and third-generation PIs tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparative data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The P1'/R1 position change to the larger 2-ethyl-n-butyl moiety (R1-2) increased potency against the I84V mutant protease relative to DRV and the intermediate sized R1-1 moiety.
source: Second, the P1'/R1 position change to the larger 2-ethyl-n-butyl moiety (R1-2, UMASS-6) increased potency against the I84V mutant protease relative to DRV and the intermediate sized R1-1 moiety UMASS-1 (all three share the same R2-1 moiety); this enhanced potency of the R1-2 inhibitors over the R1-1 inhibitors was also apparent for UMASS-8 over UMASS-3, which share the same R2-3 structure (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Four of the inhibitors with the R2 moieties R2-2 or R2-5 were significantly more potent (UMASS-2, -5, -7, -10) than with the other R2 moieties.
source: Third, four of the inhibitors with the R2 moieties R2-2 or R2-5 were significantly more potent (UMASS-2, -5, -7, -10) than with the other R2 moieties.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Table 1.

claim: The trend of increased potency for R2-2 and R2-5 containing inhibitors was most pronounced for activity against the I50V/A71V mutant enzyme in both the R1-1 and R1-2 backgrounds.
source: This trend was most pronounced for activity against the I50V/A71V mutant enzyme in both the R1-1 and R1-2 backgrounds (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both the R1 and R2 constituents contribute to potency, and to enhancing potency over DRV.
source: The significant potency of the R2-2 and R2-5 containing inhibitors against the I50V/A71V mutant enzyme while maintaining good potency against the I84V enzyme indicates that both the R1 and R2 constituents contribute to potency, and to enhancing potency over DRV.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Ki data patterns.

claim: The EC50 values of the R2-2 and R2-5 containing inhibitors were among the lowest measured.
source: This potency was also seen in inhibition of viral infectivity as the EC50 values of the R2-2 and R2-5 containing inhibitors were among the lowest measured (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: All of the selections starting with wild-type virus reached at least 5 µM of inhibitor concentration.
source: All of the selections starting with wild-type virus reached at least 5 µM of inhibitor concentration (approximating the therapeutic concentration reached by DRV in the blood and in the range of a 1000-fold increase in the starting EC50).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the selection experiments.

claim: Only five of the selections starting with the mixture of mutants reached an inhibitor concentration as high as 400 nM.
source: For technical reasons, only five of the selections starting with the mixture of mutants reached an inhibitor concentration as high as 400 nM and are reported here (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text describing the selection experiments.

claim: For selections that reached 5 μM, 8–14 mutations were present in the most abundant variant.
source: For those selections that reached 5 μM, 8–14 mutations were present in the most abundant variant.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 2A.

claim: On average the three most abundant variants in the 5 μM cultures accounted for 88% of the total viral population.
source: Typically the next two most abundant variants in the population differed by a single amino acid, and on average the three most abundant variants in the 5 μM cultures accounted for 88% of the total viral population (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Evolution of resistance followed two pathways, one based on I50V and one based on I84V.
source: Evolution of resistance followed two pathways, one based on I50V and one based on I84V.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 2A.

claim: In three cultures (V2wt, V5wt, and V2mut), the I84V and I50V mutations became linked on the same genome.
source: In three cultures, V2wt, V5wt, and V2mut (which reached either 4 or 5 μM final drug concentration; V2wt indicates the virus pool selected with UMASS-2 starting with wild-type virus), these two mutations, I84V and I50V, became linked on the same genome (Figure 2A) showing they are not mutually exclusive
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 2A.

claim: The I84V and I50V mutations are not mutually exclusive.
source: In three cultures, V2wt, V5wt, and V2mut (which reached either 4 or 5 μM final drug concentration; V2wt indicates the virus pool selected with UMASS-2 starting with wild-type virus), these two mutations, I84V and I50V, became linked on the same genome (Figure 2A) showing they are not mutually exclusive
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of linked mutations.

claim: The appearance of the linked I84V/I50V mutations occurred in the selections of the UMASS inhibitors (-2 and -5) that showed the greatest potency against the two mutant enzymes I84V and I50V/A71V.
source: it is worth noting that the appearance of the linked I84V/I50V mutations occurred in the selections of the UMASS inhibitors (-2 and -5) that showed the greatest potency against the two mutant enzymes I84V and I50V/A71V (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), consistent with inhibitor potency driving the co-selection of these two primary resistance mutations together.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Inhibitor potency drives the co-selection of the I84V and I50V primary resistance mutations together.
source: it is worth noting that the appearance of the linked I84V/I50V mutations occurred in the selections of the UMASS inhibitors (-2 and -5) that showed the greatest potency against the two mutant enzymes I84V and I50V/A71V (Table 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), consistent with inhibitor potency driving the co-selection of these two primary resistance mutations together.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between inhibitor potency and linked mutations.

claim: The number of mutations present at 100 nM drug concentration was approximately half the number present after selection to greater than 1 μM.
source: First, as can be seen in Figure 2B, the number of mutations present at 100 nM drug concentration was approximately half the number present after selection to greater than 1 μM.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: On average there were more mutations in the I50V viruses at the intermediate drug concentration (100 nM) compared to the I84V viruses.
source: In comparing the number of mutations present in cultures using the I84V versus the I50V pathway, we noted that on average there were more mutations in the I50V viruses at the intermediate drug concentration compared to the I84V viruses (100 nM, p=0.03), and this trend continued at the higher drug concentration.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by statistical analysis of data in Figure 2B.

claim: Resistance (measured as an increase in the EC50) was apparent after selection to the 100 nM inhibitor concentration.
source: As can be seen in Figure 2C, resistance (measured as an increase in the EC50) was apparent after selection to the 100 nM inhibitor concentration, and in each case the EC50 increased an average of 100-fold after selection to the final inhibitor concentration of 5 μM (EC50 values of the final virus pool are shown in Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C and Table 1.

claim: The EC50 increased an average of 100-fold after selection to the final inhibitor concentration of 5 μM.
source: As can be seen in Figure 2C, resistance (measured as an increase in the EC50) was apparent after selection to the 100 nM inhibitor concentration, and in each case the EC50 increased an average of 100-fold after selection to the final inhibitor concentration of 5 μM (EC50 values of the final virus pool are shown in Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C and Table 1.

claim: Selection to 100 nM inhibitor concentration resulted in a reduction in fitness/relative infectivity by between 100- and 1000-fold.
source: As can be seen in Figure 2D, selection to 100 nM inhibitor concentration resulted in a reduction in fitness/relative infectivity by between 100- and 1000-fold.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: Cultures with the biggest decrease in fitness rebounded to around 1% relative infectivity after selection to an inhibitor level of 5 μM.
source: Those cultures with the biggest decrease in fitness rebounded to around 1% relative infectivity after selection to an inhibitor level of 5 μM.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: High levels of resistance are linked to maintaining a residual level of relative infectivity around 1%.
source: This suggests that these high levels of resistance are linked to maintaining a residual level of relative infectivity around 1% (as defined under these culture conditions).
evidence: This is an inference based on the fitness data.

claim: There is a strong relationship between higher Ki values (i.e., resistance) and dramatic reductions in catalytic efficiency.
source: As can be seen, there is a strong relationship between higher Ki values (i.e., resistance) and dramatic reductions in catalytic efficiency, consistent with the loss of fitness associated with these viral populations.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: The loss of catalytic efficiency is consistent with the loss of fitness associated with resistant viral populations.
source: As can be seen, there is a strong relationship between higher Ki values (i.e., resistance) and dramatic reductions in catalytic efficiency, consistent with the loss of fitness associated with these viral populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between Ki and catalytic efficiency.

claim: Each of the viral cultures started with wild-type virus showed an accumulation of protease mutations with increasing selective pressure.
source: Each of the viral cultures started with wild-type virus showed an accumulation of protease mutations with increasing selective pressure.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data in Figure 3A.

claim: NGS analysis revealed very few fixed variants in the cultures started with wild-type virus until the inhibitor concentration reached approximately 3–5 nM.
source: NGS analysis revealed very few fixed variants in the cultures started with wild-type virus until the inhibitor concentration reached approximately 3–5 nM (approaching the EC50 value for the wild-type virus, Table 1)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data in Figure 3A.

claim: The cultures that were started with the mutant library selected for the outgrowth of a subset of those mutants by 1 nM inhibitor concentration.
source: in contrast, the cultures that were started with the mutant library selected for the outgrowth of a subset of those mutants by 1 nM inhibitor concentration (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data in Figure 3A.

claim: The transition through the EC50 concentration of the wild-type virus provided significant selective pressure for fixing mutations.
source: In all cultures, the transition through the EC50 concentration of the wild-type virus provided significant selective pressure for fixing mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data in Figure 3A.

claim: Multiple unfixed mutations were observed in each culture after the drug concentration exceeded the EC50 values above 3 nM, highlighting the high genetic diversity in the culture.
source: Multiple unfixed mutations were observed in each culture after the drug concentration exceeded the EC50 values above 3 nM, highlighting the high genetic diversity in the culture.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data in Figure 3A.

claim: Additional mutations became linked on each viral genome at higher drug concentrations.
source: Additional mutations became linked on each viral genome at higher drug concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data.

claim: In the cultures that showed the early appearance of the I84V mutation, this was associated with a peak in entropy, reflecting high genetic diversity, followed by a decrease in entropy when the I84V mutation became fixed.
source: In the cultures that showed the early appearance of the I84V mutation, this was associated with a peak in entropy, reflecting high genetic diversity, followed by a decrease in entropy when the I84V mutation became fixed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by entropy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The introduction of the I50V mutation was generally not associated with a drop in entropy, rather these populations maintained high genetic diversity even at higher drug concentrations.
source: The introduction of the I50V mutation was generally not associated with a drop in entropy, rather these populations maintained high genetic diversity even at higher drug concentrations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by entropy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: I84V confers some level of resistance without a dramatic loss in fitness, allowing a more homogeneous culture (i.e., less entropy).
source: We interpret these patterns as indicative of I84V conferring some level of resistance without a dramatic loss in fitness, allowing a more homogeneous culture (i.e., less entropy).
evidence: This is an interpretation/inference based on the entropy patterns.

claim: I50V may confer a higher level of resistance but at a greater fitness cost, thus supporting greater diversity in the culture either as compensatory mutations or as other combinations of mutations with lesser resistance but higher fitness.
source: In contrast, I50V may confer a higher level of resistance but at a greater fitness cost, thus supporting greater diversity in the culture either as compensatory mutations or as other combinations of mutations with lesser resistance but higher fitness.
evidence: This is an interpretation/inference based on the entropy patterns.

claim: I50V significantly reduces the fitness of the virus relative to the fitness loss of a virus with I84V as single mutations.
source: In this regard, we previously showed I50V significantly reduces the fitness of the virus relative to the fitness loss of a virus with I84V as single mutations (Henderson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Cultures starting with the mixture of resistant viruses averaged a nearly twofold higher entropy value compared to the cultures where the selection started with just the virus generated from the NL4-3/wild-type clone (3.0 vs. 1.6, p<0.0001 Mann–Whitney test).
source: When we examined the sequence diversity as assessed by Shannon entropy for all selections that reached at least 1 µM in inhibitor concentration, we found that cultures starting with the mixture of resistant viruses averaged a nearly twofold higher entropy value compared to the cultures where the selection started with just the virus generated from the NL4-3/wild-type clone (3.0 vs. 1.6, p<0.0001 Mann–Whitney test; Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by statistical analysis of entropy data in Figure 3B–D.

claim: The higher entropy in cultures starting with mutant mixtures is most easily explained if the rates of recombination were fairly high throughout the culture period so that most sequence variants were maintained at least at a low level.
source: This result is most easily explained if the rates of recombination were fairly high throughout the culture period so that most sequence variants were maintained at least at a low level.
evidence: This is an inference/speculation to explain the entropy difference.

claim: At the end of the selection period no wild-type variants could be detected in the cultures by deep sequencing.
source: However, at the end of the selection period no wild-type variants could be detected in the cultures by deep sequencing.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NGS data.

claim: The R1 group largely defined the resistance pathway observed.
source: We found that the R1 group, that is, the (S)-2-methylbutyl (R1-1) or the 2-ethyl-n-butyl (R1-2), largely defined the resistance pathway observed
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by analysis of selection outcomes.

claim: With the UMASS-1 through -5 series (the smaller R1-1 group), the I84V mutation appeared first in six of seven cultures.
source: With the UMASS-1 through -5 series (the smaller R1-1 group), the I84V mutation appeared first in six of seven cultures.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data.

claim: With the UMASS-6 through -10 series with the larger R1-2 group, the I50V mutation appeared first in eight of nine cultures (p=0.009, Fisher's exact test).
source: In contrast, the UMASS-6 through -10 series with the larger R1-2 group, the I50V mutation appeared first in eight of nine cultures (p=0.009, Fisher's exact test; in this analysis, we included two cultures that did not reach at least 400 nM inhibitor concentration but did fix an initial set of mutations to increase our sample size [V3mut, V5mut], and we did not include two cultures where both I84V and I50V were initially fixed together [V2wt, V5wt]).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by statistical analysis of sequencing data.

claim: In only one of the eight cultures with sufficient data from both selections was there a switch from the I84V pathway to the I50V pathway between the first and second selections.
source: However, in only one of the eight cultures with sufficient data from both selections was there a switch from the I84V pathway to the I50V pathway between the first and second selections (cultures of UMASS-6 with an R1-2 group).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data.

claim: The P1'-equivalent chemical structure of the inhibitor is a strong determinant of the resistance pathway selected.
source: Thus, we conclude that the P1'-equivalent chemical structure of the inhibitor is a strong determinant of the resistance pathway selected.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of selection outcomes.

claim: One inhibitor could select for different pathways in two separate selections even when both major mutations are maintained in the viral population.
source: It is notable that one inhibitor could select for different pathways in two separate selections (also seen with DRV, see Figure 2—figure supplement 4) even when both major mutations are maintained in the viral population (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in figures.

claim: Either pathway can provide some level of resistance to most if not all of these inhibitors.
source: This suggests that either pathway can provide some level of resistance to most if not all of these inhibitors, and that the chance addition of the initial compensatory mutations may determine which pathway becomes the major resistant population.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of pathway variability.

claim: The chance addition of the initial compensatory mutations may determine which pathway becomes the major resistant population.
source: This suggests that either pathway can provide some level of resistance to most if not all of these inhibitors, and that the chance addition of the initial compensatory mutations may determine which pathway becomes the major resistant population.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of pathway variability.

claim: Several mutations are uniquely linked or at least strongly favored in the I84V pathway, with I84V being linked to V32I.
source: Several mutations are uniquely linked or at least strongly favored in each pathway, with I84V being linked to V32I, and I50V being linked to I47V, F53L, and I13V.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by analysis of pooled sequencing data in Figure 4A.

claim: I50V is linked to I47V, F53L, and I13V.
source: Several mutations are uniquely linked or at least strongly favored in each pathway, with I84V being linked to V32I, and I50V being linked to I47V, F53L, and I13V.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by analysis of pooled sequencing data in Figure 4A.

claim: A number of mutations appear in both pathways, although not with equal frequency: L10F, L33F, M46I, I54L, A71V, and V82I.
source: A number of mutations appear in both pathways, although not with equal frequency: L10F, L33F, M46I, I54L, A71V, and V82I.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by analysis of pooled sequencing data in Figure 4A.

claim: While some mutations are largely linked to one pathway, other mutations are often shared between the two pathways.
source: These results show that while some mutations are largely linked to one pathway, other mutations are often shared between the two pathways.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the analysis of mutation patterns.

claim: The variation in frequency of appearance of shared mutations in the two pathways suggests different levels of impact on resistance and/or fitness in the I84V vs. the I50V background for these mutations.
source: Also, the variation in frequency of appearance of shared mutations in the two pathways suggests different levels of impact on resistance and/or fitness in the I84V vs. the I50V background for these mutations (e.g., L10F, M46I and A71V).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential frequency of mutations.

claim: The larger impact of I50V on fitness compared to I84V mutations is consistent with the earlier appearance and greater levels of fixation of the shared compensatory mutations L10F, L33F, M46I, and A71V in the cultures that followed the I50V pathway.
source: In particular, the larger impact of I50V on fitness compared to I84V mutations (Henderson et al., 2012) is consistent with the earlier appearance and greater levels of fixation of the shared compensatory mutations L10F, L33F, M46I, and A71V in the cultures that followed the I50V pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutation patterns and cited fitness data.

claim: There are stochastic elements in the selection process that make each culture different in detail but by pooling the data across the cultures underlying patterns are apparent.
source: These results emphasize that there are stochastic elements in the selection process that make each culture different in detail but that by pooling the data across the cultures underlying patterns are apparent.

claim: The inhibitors with the smaller R1-1 group showed a trend to be less potent than the inhibitors with the larger R1-2 group when tested against all of the resistant proteases.

claim: Inhibitors with the R2-2 group showed a trend toward greater residual potency against the mutant enzymes compared to the other inhibitors.
source: Inhibitors with the R2-2 group showed a trend toward greater residual potency against the mutant enzymes compared to the other inhibitors (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Figure 5B.

claim: The highly resistant enzymes with the I84V mutation remained more sensitive to the entire group of inhibitors than the enzymes with the I50V mutation.
source: In looking at the individual pathways, the highly resistant enzymes with the I84V mutation remained more sensitive to the entire group of inhibitors than the enzymes with the I50V mutation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Figure 5C.

claim: The resistant proteases with I50V had similar Ki values to both the R1-1 and R1-2 inhibitors, while the proteases with I84V were more sensitive (lower Ki) to the larger R1-2 inhibitors.
source: The resistant proteases with I50V had similar Ki values to both the R1-1 and R1-2 inhibitors, while the proteases with I84V were more sensitive (lower Ki) to the larger R1-2 inhibitors (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Figure 5D.

claim: The increased potency of the R2-2 inhibitors over the rest of the inhibitors was seen against the enzymes carrying I84V but not those with I50V.
source: Similarly, the increased potency of the R2-2 inhibitors over the rest of the inhibitors was seen against the enzymes carrying I84V but not those with I50V (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Ki data in Figure 5E.

claim: The smaller R1-1 inhibitors selecting for the I84V pathway and the larger R1-2 inhibitors selecting for the I50V pathway is consistent with the R2-2 inhibitors adding additional potency that is retained even after selection for resistance, most apparent with the I84V pathway.
source: These results are consistent with the smaller R1-1 inhibitors selecting for the I84V pathway and the larger R1-2 inhibitors selecting for the I50V pathway, and with the R2-2 inhibitors adding additional potency that is retained even after selection for resistance, most apparent with the I84V pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Ki data patterns.

claim: When the EC50 values against the virus pools using the I84V or the I50V pathway were compared for all of the inhibitors, the inhibitors with the larger R1-2 group were more potent, retaining on average lower EC50 values compared to the EC50 values for the inhibitors with the smaller R1-1 group.
source: When the EC50 values against the virus pools using the I84V or the I50V pathway were compared for all of the inhibitors, the inhibitors with the larger R1-2 group were more potent, retaining on average lower EC50 values compared to the EC50 values for the inhibitors with the smaller R1-1 group (Figure 6A).

claim: Inhibitors with the R2-2 group showed a trend toward greater potency compared to the other R2 groups in viral assays.
source: Inhibitors with the R2-2 group showed a trend toward greater potency compared to the other R2 groups (Figure 6B), consistent with what was observed in enzymatic assays.

claim: Viruses in the I50V pathway had a higher level of resistance to these inhibitors than the viruses in the I84V pathway.
source: When we considered the effects based on the selection pathway, we observed that viruses in the I50V pathway had a higher level of resistance to these inhibitors than the viruses in the I84V pathway (Figure 6C).

claim: The higher level of resistance for the viruses using the I50V pathway was due to the fact that these viruses were similarly resistant to the inhibitors with either the R1-1 or the R1-2 groups.
source: The higher level of resistance for the viruses using the I50V pathway was due to the fact that these viruses were similarly resistant to the inhibitors with either the R1-1 or the R1-2 groups; in contrast, the viruses using the I84V pathway conferred a greater level of resistance to the inhibitors with the smaller R1-1 group while the inhibitors with the larger R1-2 group retained a higher level of potency (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by EC50 data in Figure 6D.

claim: There was a trend for viruses in either pathway to be less resistant to the inhibitors with the R2-2 group.
source: Finally, there was a trend for viruses in either pathway to be less resistant to the inhibitors with the R2-2 group (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by EC50 data in Figure 6E.

claim: DRV has a butyl group at the R1 position, smaller than the R1-1 methylbutyl in the UMASS-1 through -5 series.
source: DRV has a butyl group at the R1 position, smaller than the R1-1 methylbutyl in the UMASS-1 through -5 series.

source: Thus, four of five independent selection with DRV favored the resistance pathway I84V, associated with a smaller R1 constituent.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data from DRV selections.

claim: The DRV selection results add further evidence for the size of the R1 moiety strongly influencing the resistance pathway.
source: These results add further evidence for the size of the R1 moiety strongly influencing the resistance pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the DRV selection data.

claim: Cleavage site mutations are seen during selection for resistance to protease inhibitors.
source: Cleavage site mutations are seen during selection for resistance to protease inhibitors (Su et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The effect of cleavage site mutations is most apparent at the cleavage sites flanking the spacer peptide SP2 in Gag (NC/SP2 and SP2/p6).
source: This can be viewed as protease-substrate coevolution, and the effect is most apparent at the cleavage sites flanking the spacer peptide SP2 in Gag (NC/SP2 and SP2/p6) (Kolli et al., 2006; Kolli et al., 2014; Kolli et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2012; Özen et al., 2011; Özen et al., 2012; Özen et al., 2014; Prabu-Jeyabalan et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: An analysis of four cultures that had I84V as the major resistance mutation showed they all had a mutation at the NC/SP2 cleavage site at position P2, with a change from the wild-type alanine amino acid to either of the larger aliphatic amino acids valine or isoleucine.
source: An analysis of four cultures that had I84V as the major resistance mutation showed they all had a mutation at the NC/SP2 cleavage site at position P2, with a change from the wild-type alanine amino acid to either of the larger aliphatic amino acids valine or isoleucine.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: Three of the four I84V cultures had a mutation at the adjacent SP2/p6 cleavage site, either at P1' (leucine to phenylalanine) or P5' (proline to leucine).
source: In addition, three of the four I84V cultures had a mutation at the adjacent SP2/p6 cleavage site, either at P1' (leucine to phenylalanine) or P5' (proline to leucine).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: All seven cultures where the I50V mutation was the major resistance mutation had a mutation in the SP2/p6 cleavage site, but not in the NC/SP2 site.
source: Conversely, all seven cultures where the I50V mutation was the major resistance mutation there was a mutation in the SP2/p6 cleavage site, but not in the NC/SP2 site.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A.

source: Finally, in the three cultures where the protease evolved both the I50V and I84V mutations, Gag mutations were observed only at the SP2/p6 cleavage site (the presence or absence of the NC/SP2 mutation in the I84V cultures but not in the I84V/I50V cultures has a p value of 0.03 in a Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A and statistical analysis.

claim: Two of three cultures with both I84V and I50V had both the P1' (leucine to phenylalanine) and P5' (proline to leucine) mutations.
source: Two of three cultures with both I84V and I50V had both the P1' (leucine to phenylalanine) and P5' (proline to leucine) mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: Mutations at both P1' and P5' together were underrepresented in the cultures with only I50V.
source: In contrast, mutations at both P1' and P5' together were underrepresented in the cultures with only I50V.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: The NC/SP2 mutation at P2 in the presence of the I84V mutation may engage I50 to replace the lost interaction with I84V as it moves away from the P2 sidechain by shortening (I to V).

source: this would explain the absence of this cleavage site mutation in the double protease mutant (I50V/I84V) since the shortening of both protease sidechains provides too little interaction with the longer P2 sidechain.

claim: The P1' and P5' mutations in the SP2/P6 site appear to act in a complementary way as typically only one is seen with either the I50V or the I84V mutant proteases.
source: The P1' and P5' mutations in the SP2/P6 site appear to act in a complementary way as typically only one is seen with either the I50V or the I84V mutant proteases (Figure 7C).

claim: The SP2/p6 P1' and P5' mutations engage the protease by different mechanisms suggesting their effects are additive.
source: The SP2/p6 P1' and P5' mutations engage the protease by different mechanisms (Özen et al., 2014) suggesting their effects are additive
evidence: This is an inference based on cited previous work.

claim: The single mutation at P1' or P5' may be sufficient to recover an appropriate rate of cleavage with either the I84V or the I50V mutant protease, but the additive effects of the P1' and P5' mutations may be needed to rescue cleavage by the I50V/I84V mutant protease.
source: thus in these selections the single mutation at P1' or P5' may be sufficient to recover an appropriate rate of cleavage with either the I84V or the I50V mutant protease, but the additive effects of the P1' and P5' mutations may be needed to rescue cleavage by the I50V/I84V mutant protease.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutation patterns and structural considerations.

claim: DRV represents a potent antiviral due in large part to its ability to achieve drug levels in the blood that are far above the EC50 and the fact that high-level resistance requires many mutations (a high genetic barrier).
source: DRV represents a potent antiviral due in large part to its ability to achieve drug levels in the blood that are far above the EC50 and the fact that high-level resistance requires many mutations (a high genetic barrier).
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion.

claim: Resistance to DRV usually follows the less deleterious I84V pathway.
source: However, we have shown that resistance usually follows the less deleterious I84V pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the selection experiments.

claim: The UMASS-2 inhibitor anchors the R2-2 group to the protease backbone and allows the intermediate-sized R1-1 group to co-select both the I84V and I50V pathways, creating an even higher genetic bar.
source: The UMASS-2 inhibitor anchors the R2-2 group to the protease backbone and allows the intermediate-sized R1-1 group to co-select both the I84V and I50V pathways, creating an even higher genetic bar.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the selection experiments and structural analysis.

claim: The enhanced potency of UMASS-2 could potentially be traded for reduced maximum drug levels allowing a given mass of drug to provide antiviral coverage for a longer period of time.
source: The enhanced potency of UMASS-2 could potentially be traded for reduced maximum drug levels allowing a given mass of drug to provide antiviral coverage for a longer period of time.
evidence: This is speculation about potential clinical applications.

claim: The P1'/R1-1 group is directed at the protease I84 sidechain, consistent with the shortening of this sidechain as a major resistance mechanism.
source: As we have previously discussed (Lockbaum et al., 2019; Mittal et al., 2013), in these structures it is apparent that the P1'/R1-1 group is directed at the protease I84 sidechain, consistent with the shortening of this sidechain as a major resistance mechanism.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by structural data and citations.

claim: The longer P1'/R1-2 group is oriented into the space between I84 and I50, thus drawing in I50V as the pathway to resistance.
source: Conversely, the longer P1'/R1-2 group is oriented into the space between I84 and I50, thus drawing in I50V as the pathway to resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by structural data in Figure 8A-C.

claim: The I50V resistance pathway presents additional challenges to the virus in the more rapid accumulation of compensatory mutations.
source: As noted in the longitudinal analysis of the selection pathway, the I50V resistance pathway presents additional challenges to the virus in the more rapid accumulation of compensatory mutations (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Under the circumstances of rapidly declining viral load during the initiation of therapy, the need for additional mutations in the I50V pathway would represent an enhanced genetic barrier.
source: Under the circumstances of rapidly declining viral load during the initiation of therapy, this need for additional mutations would represent an enhanced genetic barrier.
evidence: This is an inference about clinical implications.

claim: The less potent inhibitors interact with the protease side chains and backbone at D29 and D30 through a network of water molecules.
source: The less potent inhibitors interact with the protease side chains and backbone at D29 and D30 through a network of water molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by structural data in Figure 8D.

source: In contrast, with the more potent R2-2 group the water molecules are replaced with direct interactions between inhibitor and protease in the S2' subsite (Figure 8E).

source: This direct interaction more closely mimics the interaction made by the glutamine P2' side chain in the optimized protease cleavage site at the SP1/NC boundary (Figure 8F).

source: Thus, the ability to replace the water-mediated interactions with a more rigid framework that is interacting with the protease backbone deep in the S2' pocket appears to be a unique feature of the inhibitors with R2-2.

claim: Improved potency in another series of PIs was also reported for the R2-2 P2' moiety.
source: Improved potency in another series of PIs was also reported for this R2-2 P2' moiety (Zhu et al., 2020).

claim: The two inhibitors with the greatest potency as enzymes (UMASS-2 and UMASS-5) were the only inhibitors that selected for I84V and I50V linked on the same genome.
source: While the different R2 structures did not select for any novel resistance mutations, we did note that the two inhibitors with the greatest potency as enzymes (UMASS-2 and UMASS-5) were the only inhibitors that selected for I84V and I50V linked on the same genome (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 2A.

claim: Anchoring to the backbone with R2-2 for UMASS-2 may make the R1-1 group less mobile, reducing the magnitude of the effect of the I84V mutation allowing the inhibitor to maintain some level of interaction with I50.
source: It is possible that anchoring to the backbone with R2-2 for UMASS-2 makes the R1-1 group less mobile, reducing the magnitude of the effect of the I84V mutation allowing the inhibitor to maintain some level of interaction with I50, although this inference was not tested directly.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Resistance mutations that were detected in multiple selections summed to at least 16 positions.
source: Resistance mutations that were detected in multiple selections summed to at least 16 positions (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by sequencing data in Figure 2A.

claim: The linked compensatory mutations (V32I with I84V, and I47V/F53L with I50V) are each close to the primary resistance mutation, suggesting they interact directly with the primary resistance mutation to adjust its position within the subsite to limit interaction with the inhibitor and/or improve interaction with the substrate.
source: These linked compensatory mutations are each close to the primary resistance mutation, suggesting they interact directly with the primary resistance mutation to adjust its position within the subsite to limit interaction with the inhibitor and/or improve interaction with the substrate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural proximity of mutations.

claim: Mutations distal from the active site modulate the enzymatic activity and fitness by altering the dynamic ensemble of the enzyme.
source: In contrast to the linked compensatory mutations, the shared compensatory mutations are often more distant in the structure from the primary resistance mutation. Mutations distal from the active site modulate the enzymatic activity and fitness by altering the dynamic ensemble (Foulkes-Murzycki et al., 2007; Henes et al., 2019; Leidner et al., 2021; Ragland et al., 2014; Ragland et al., 2017; Whitfield et al., 2020) of the enzyme (i.e., conformations sampled).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Distal mutations can sometimes enhance enzymatic activity, but they also often significantly contribute to high levels of resistance.
source: While these changes can sometimes enhance enzymatic activity, they also often significantly contribute to high levels of resistance (Henes et al., 2019; Matthew et al., 2021) as is observed in these selections.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and data from this study.

source: As can be seen in Figure 2E, there is a strong correlation between increasing resistance (lower Ki) and lost catalytic efficiency (larger kcat/Km).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2E.

source: This suggests that compensatory mutations may attenuate fitness loss but do not restore it, or they impact resistance, or both.

source: In Figure 4B, it can be seen that the same compensatory mutation is part of two different resistance pathways but with differing selective pressure to add the mutation, hinting at the complexity of the role of such mutations and their pathway-specific contributions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4B.

evidence: This is stated in the text based on database analysis.

source: For sequences associated with a greater than 200-fold change in resistance to DRV, there were an average of 5.4 resistance-associated mutations (with a maximum of seven mutations).
